newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom-From Reichspost to global player.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom-From Reichspost to global player.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG, now embarked on Europe's largest ever privatisation, has evolved into a major force on the global telecommunications after more than 100 years as a regional phone monopoly originating with the imperial Reichspost under Kaiser Wilhelm I.
Here is a brief history of Deutsche Telekom:

1996: October 21, Telekom sets share price between 25 and 30 marks. October 22, subscription period for initial public offering begins. To end on November 14. Shares to begin trading in Germany and New York on November 18, Tokyo a day later.
- October 11, share information centre closes with over three million registrations.
- July, German telecommunications act passed creating framework for competition in 1998.
- March 20, Telekom opens information centre and registation for private investors interested in share issue.
1996: Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint Corp of the United States form joint venture Global One.
- Deutsche Telekom rate reform takes effect. Higher local charges unleashes storm of public protest.
1995: October 30, Telekom says it will issue shares to public in November 1996.
- Deutsche Bundespost Telekom becomes stock company owned by the federal government. Renamed Deutsche Telekom AG.
1993: European Union issues directive ending all monopolies over basic telephone services by January 1, 1998.
1993: Telekom und France Telecom form global outsourcing venture Eunetcom as basis of strategic alliance.
1992: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel announces planned privatisation of Telekom.
1991: Telekom begins building D1 digital cellular GSM network in competition to Mannesmann.

1990: German unification merges former East German phone authority with Deutsche Bundespost Telekom. Telekom launches nearly 60 billion mark investment programme to upgrade dilapidated east German phone system.
- Telekom loses monopoly over sale of phone equipment.
- Deutsche Bundespost Telekom forms subsidiaries in New York, London, Tokyo und Brussels. The first fibre optical cable is connected to a private home in Germany.
- Postal reform takes effect, creating Deutsche Bundespost Telekom as government agency.
1989: Introduction of Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN), a high speed digital communications network.
- German government awards first private licence to Mannesmann AG to build and operate digital cellular phone service based on European-developed GSM standard.
1984: German online computer service Btx started.
1979: West Germany begins offering telefax services.
1965: Communications satellite "Early Bird" put in orbit. First computers connected via modems over normal phone line.
1955: First international direct-dialling service started.
1950: Deutsche Bundespost is formed as part of the Federal Post Ministry in postwar West Germany.
1924: Largely independent company Deutsche Reichspost evolves from ministry.
1881: First public telephone network.
1877: Reichspost makes first successful phone connection in Germany over a distance of two km using Bell telephones. -- Claus Hulverscheidt, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 2609750
